correctness.rationale: All possible strict open-cell masks are exactly 0<=k<1/c, the unweighted clique graph-Laplacian Gram form for each nonzero mask decomposes orthogonally into an active contrast eigenvalue n (k>=2), a rank-one eigenvalue (n-k)[1+kc(nc-2)], and zero modes. Every admissible cell has a strictly positive interior point. Global piecewise-affine segment bounds and local real singular-vector witnesses establish the exact norm on the complex domain by modulus contraction. The c=1/2 limit uses only feasible k=1,2 and yields the stated n-specific discontinuity. The checker replayed 214 exact rational Gram identities, 14400 real and 1500 complex direct pair comparisons and 18 jump tests; the proof, not samples, handles all n and real alpha.

value.rationale: The exact nonlinear pairwise l2-to-graph-energy sensitivity of a canonical fractional maximal operator is a motivated perturbation-robustness invariant, not merely its one-input variation. The k<1/c constraint yields a nontrivial sharp spectral classification for every clique dimension and fractional exponent, with a surprising discontinuous parameter transition at c=1/2 in every n>=3 except n=5; such jumps matter for assessing noise sensitivity in fractional graph averaging. The complete all-dimensional formula and boundary mechanism are more informative than an arbitrary finite calculation.
